clue.text: A physics qualification, say, is spun as quantity on graph

parts.note: a BSc, Bachelor of Science, is a degree a physicist might hold; 'say' marks it as an example
taken as written

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the little word as is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before the turn

explanation.surface: Someone describes a physics degree being talked up, spun, as a measure on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spun' turns AS into SA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph the abscissa is the horizontal coordinate, a measured quantity plotted along the x-axis.

clue.text: Fainting is a shortcoming in fight

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other here

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing
a lack is a shortcoming or deficiency

explanation.surface: Passing out is a weakness in a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a temporary loss of consciousness, a spell of fainting.

clue.text: Way of mixing film in snappy clip

parts.note: snappy means irritable, cross
to clip is to cut

explanation.surface: A film editor's technique hidden in a short, crisp clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-cutting is a film-editing technique alternating shots of two scenes, a way of intercutting footage.

clue.text: It's mildly disappointing having Victoria's location unknown

parts.note: London's Victoria station is in the SW1 postcode, with the 1 read as the letter I
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Being unable to find Victoria station is a bit of a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postal district round Victoria; its figure 1 doubles as the letter I. A swiz is British slang for a swindle or letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiz is informal British slang for a disappointment or minor swindle, something mildly disappointing.

clue.text: Fruity colour, a mostly loud affair

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: vocal means loud, outspoken
a do is a party or affair

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fruit-coloured, rather noisy party.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a greenish colour named after the fruit's flesh or skin.

clue.text: Disloyal quality, not tight (not initially)

parts.note: a trait is a quality or characteristic

indicators.note: not initially means dropping the opening letter of the word

parts.note: porous means letting water through, not watertight

explanation.surface: A disloyal character trait, said to be loose rather than tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes P from POROUS, leaving OROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitorous describes behaviour that betrays, synonym for disloyal or treacherous.

clue.text: Possibly a dab hand at induction coiling with a winding

definitions.text: Possibly a dab hand at induction

indicators.note: winding suggests twisting the letters round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Electrical induction coils call for a skilled hand to wind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Induction' looks electrical, matching the coils, but means logical reasoning from cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A logician is an expert in reasoning, including induction, so possibly a dab hand at it.

clue.text: Air — tiny bit lifting as I fly?

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a drib is a tiny amount, as in dribs and drabs

explanation.surface: A tune flies up as I take wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns DRIB into BIRD. The definition is the songbird speaking: what flies, and sings?
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird is a singing bird, one that could say of itself that it flies.

clue.text: Turn string of solos out, rivalling musical star

indicators.note: turn means the run of letters is read backwards
a string of letters is pulled out of consecutive words

explanation.surface: A performer delivers a string of solos and outshines the rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string of' picks OSOUTRIV from 'solos out, rivalling' and 'Turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a brilliantly skilled performer, especially a star musician.

clue.text: Ally worrying on withdrawal of US colt?

parts.note: a pal is a friend or ally

indicators.note: withdrawal of means these letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: ominous means threatening, worrying
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend frets as an American racehorse is pulled from the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawal of US' leaves OMINO from OMINOUS. The question mark shows a colt is only one example of the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A palomino is a golden horse with a pale mane, so a colt could be one.

clue.text: Striking sharply, caught rim with high sound

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a lip is a rim or edge
a ping is a short high-pitched sound

explanation.surface: A ball struck hard catches the rim with a ringing note.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping means hitting smartly, as in clipping someone round the ear.

clue.text: Dubious, bright bird consuming hot dog that's off

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a toucan is a brightly coloured tropical bird
H stands for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A colourful bird swallows a hot dog that has gone bad, which is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' is part of the bird, not the definition: the toucan is famous for its vivid bill. 'Off' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch-and-go means precarious, of uncertain outcome, hence dubious.

clue.text: First inhabitant arranging oil bargain

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An early settler strikes a deal over oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An aboriginal is an original native of a land, one of its first inhabitants.

clue.text: First signs of fighting in Japan's island nation

indicators.note: first signs of means taking the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The opening shots of fighting in an island country of the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is an independent island country in the South Pacific, a nation.

clue.text: Stop boy grabbing M. Hulot

indicators.note: grabbing means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
Monsieur Hulot was the screen character created and played by Jacques Tati

explanation.surface: A boy seizes the bumbling French film hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati wrote and starred in films as the bumbling Monsieur Hulot.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a stopping place, a stop on a railway or bus route.

clue.text: Trick is singular knack with most of locks

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
to get the hang of something is to get the knack

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: locks are hair

explanation.surface: A peculiar skill with picking most kinds of locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HAIR to HAI. 'Locks' suggests door locks, but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone is to trick or force them into doing something, originally into a ship's crew.

clue.text: A blight, bug on hot tropical plant

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blight
an ant is an insect, loosely a bug
H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Pests and blight ravage a plant in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a genus of plants, many tropical, grown for grain and showy flowers.

clue.text: Man's cousin parking small car in brick box

indicators.note: in shows one word placed inside the other

parts.note: a hod is a builder's open box for carrying bricks
the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: Squeezing a small car into a builder's trough.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is the trough a bricklayer's labourer carries on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hominid is a member of the family of great apes and humans, so a relative of man.

clue.text: Going wrong, I stop fusing indium and yttrium

indicators.note: fusing means joining two elements together, with the rest set between them

parts.note: In is the chemical symbol for indium
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium
to quit is to stop

explanation.surface: A chemist gives up on fusing two metallic elements that keep failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fusing' looks like chemistry, but here it joins the two element symbols round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is wickedness, the condition of going morally wrong.

clue.text: Fantasy football originally lost by bad combination

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

indicators.note: lost by means that letter is removed from the following phrase

parts.note: fusion is a joining together, a combination

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Dreams of a football team ruined by a poor line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'football originally' is F, which is dropped from ILL FUSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is a false perception or idea, a fantasy rather than reality.

clue.text: Most favouring top bananas on mail shot

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The best bananas are posted in a mailshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' turns TOP into OPT and 'shot' turns MAIL into IMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means best or most favourable, the most favouring of outcomes.

clue.text: Trojan War champion having to grow old and abandon talking

indicators.note: talking means the words are spoken, and what is heard is what counts

parts.note: to age is to grow old and to axe is to abandon or cut

explanation.surface: A Greek hero ages and gives up speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE plus AXE, said out loud, give the hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was one of the foremost Greek warriors in the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Absurdly irrational symbol is pi

indicators.note: irrational suggests the letters are put in an illogical order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A maths joke: pi is an irrational symbol, which seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' is apt: pi is an irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Impossibly means to an absurd degree, unbelievably or absurdly.

clue.text: Good artist following suit, I'll display spray-painting

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to suit is to fit
the I of I'll gives the letter; 'll (will) display links to the definition

explanation.surface: A good painter, following suit, shows off some street art.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing or drawing on walls, often done with spray paint.

clue.text: Show a familiarity with king at this point

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
now means at this point in time

explanation.surface: A king makes a point of seeming familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to be acquainted with it, to show familiarity.

clue.text: Girl in Michigan family is a dummy

indicators.note: in shows one word placed inside the other

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
Ann is a girl's name
kin are family

explanation.surface: A girl in a Michigan family turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannikin is a model of the human figure, a tailor's or shop-window dummy.

clue.text: Gold fruit cut by a group of robots?

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A golden fruit sliced by a band of robots.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are self-operating machines, the plural of automaton, so a set of robots.

clue.text: Unscrupulous duplicity's not occupying high ground

parts.note: low means base or unscrupulous
lying is duplicity; the 's is read as is and gives no letter

explanation.surface: Dishonest double-dealing is no way to claim the moral high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High ground' suggests the moral high ground but means land at a low elevation.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-lying land is at low elevation, not occupying high ground.
